name: zsync
why: Delta-based file syncing over HTTP using rsync-like rolling checksums, a neat protocol idea behind an obscure tool.

brief.what_it_is: zsync is a command-line file transfer program that downloads a new version of a file over HTTP while reusing a copy of the older version you already have. It fetches only the changed parts, using a .zsync metadata file that the distributor generates once on the server. The input is a .zsync file plus your existing local copy; the output is the updated file. The Homebrew package installs two executables, zsync and zsyncmake.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says zsync fills a gap in large-scale file distribution: it brings rsync-style delta transfers to plain web hosting, with the rsync algorithm run on the client so the server carries no extra load. The stated target is one file on a server distributed to thousands of downloaders.
brief.how_it_works: The distributor builds a .zsync file, which holds precalculated rsync-algorithm checksums and a simple text header that can be edited, such as to change the download URL. The .zsync can point to a relative URL on the same server or to one or more absolute URLs, so third parties can offer it while still pointing at the original site. The client compares its old copy against those checksums and downloads only the new parts. The homepage does not give a command-level walkthrough.
brief.install_notes: The homepage and download index only list source tarballs (zsync-0.8.0.tar.gz is the newest, with older .tar.bz2 releases back to 0.5). They describe no build steps, dependencies, or configuration. The server-use page that would cover creating and offering .zsync files returned HTTP 404, so server setup details could not be read. A .zsync file must be generated by someone who already has the file before any client can use it.
brief.standout: Instead of the server running rsync, the client does the rsync-style work against precomputed checksums in a static .zsync file, so any plain HTTP/1.1 web server or shared hosting account can serve delta downloads. The metadata file can also be mirrored or produced by a third party.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage says the author does not do much active development these days but still reviews bug reports and pull requests on GitHub and will cut releases for interesting changes. The download index shows releases as recent as zsync-0.8.0.tar.gz (2026-08-15), with 0.7.x and 0.8.0 as rewrites. The original release was 2004 and the project never reached v1.0.
brief.caveats: Never reached v1.0. The homepage says 0.7.0 is a rewrite that is less mature than the 0.6.x line, so bugs and incompatibilities are more likely. Multiple-file (directory) support is explicitly not planned. Look-inside-compressed-file support was removed in the latest release; users who need it must use 0.6.4. It only works for files where someone has already generated a .zsync file. Licence is version 2 of the Artistic License per the homepage. The homepage was reachable but the server-use subpage was not.
quotes: zsync is a file transfer program. It allows you to download a file from a remote server, where you have a copy of an older version of the file on your computer already.
zsync requires no special server software — just a web server to host the files — and imposes no extra load on the server, making it ideal for large scale file distribution.
Client-side rsync — zsync uses the rsync algorithm, but runs it on the client side, thus avoiding the high server load associated with rsync.
